notes: The last read path is closed: a message said in a session can now be forgotten. A transcript message is a source of its own, addressed by the digest of its normalised text, and the console's session search puts a forget action next to the result - where the text is already visible, so the product prints it nowhere new. The chat command list deliberately does not offer message sources: a chat reply quoting past messages would move private text into another surface. The transcript file is never rewritten. The filter sits at every point where messages are read: the search index, the recall that runs after a fold, the session list, the per-session export, the owner profile corpus, the console's live chat history, its fork and rewind faces, the chat service's history and the command line's session view. One case is honestly different: the console's resume copies a session file byte for byte and then removes the original, so filtering that copy would destroy the last on-disk copy of the line - the copy therefore stays identical and the suppression holds on every read of the resumed file. The honest limits stay visible: the transcript line stays on disk, and so does anything already copied off this machine, committed to the public history or captured in a backup taken before the forget; normalisation makes the identity case- and whitespace-insensitive, so Hello and hello are one source and an edited message is a new one. A gate that could not run at all - the fleet browser test passed no browser executable - now resolves the cached Chromium itself, because a gate that cannot run is a gate that does not run. The counts move with the feature: 3005 core assertions and 1945 locale keys per pack. No new credential, no new outbound path, no change to any shared gateway.
